title: Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE — Premium Revision Paper #6

pages.quiz:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #6
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which pair of words is a minimal pair for /f/ and /v/? (1 mark)
   A. boy, toy
   B. cat, mat
   C. tin, chin
   D. fine, vine

2. Which of these shows how to say a word? (1 mark)
   A. The index of the atlas
   B. The page number
   C. The sound guide next to the headword
   D. The cover

3. Plural nouns: Choose the correct sentence. (1 mark)
   A. The women is selling tomatoes.
   B. The woman are selling tomatoes.
   C. The womans are selling tomatoes.
   D. The women are selling tomatoes.

4. What is the plural of 'box'? (1 mark)
   A. boxes
   B. boxies
   C. boxen
   D. boxs

5. Which word makes a request polite? (1 mark)
   A. please
   B. quick
   C. now
   D. hurry

6. Which word has the vowel /e/? (1 mark)
   A. late
   B. day
   C. pain
   D. bed

7. 'He is old enough to ride a bicycle.' Here enough comes (1 mark)
   A. before the verb
   B. at the end
   C. after the adjective
   D. before the noun

8. Which describes the letter b? (1 mark)
   A. A dot only
   B. A stick that goes below the line
   C. A round part with the stick on its right
   D. A stick with the round part on its right

9. A roundabout is (1 mark)
   A. a circular junction where vehicles go around in one direction
   B. a type of bridge
   C. a straight road
   D. a railway

10. What should you do at a railway crossing? (1 mark)
   A. Play on the track
   B. Run across
   C. Stop, look and listen
   D. Ride faster

11. A visual is something we (1 mark)
   A. taste
   B. understand by looking at it
   C. smell
   D. hear only

12. Which is a possessive pronoun? (1 mark)
   A. your
   B. you
   C. yourself
   D. yours

13. Pronouns: Which is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Ali and I went to the clinic.
   B. Ali and myself went to the clinic.
   C. Ali and me went to the clinic.
   D. Me and Ali went to the clinic.

14. Which sentence compares Kevin and Musa correctly? (1 mark)
   A. Kevin is tall than Musa.
   B. Kevin is more taller than Musa.
   C. Kevin is taller than Musa.
   D. Kevin is tallest than Musa.

15. Which detail uses the sense of smell? (1 mark)
   A. I heard a bell.
   B. I saw a table.
   C. I touched a wall.
   D. I could smell fresh bread.

16. 'A lot of' can be used with (1 mark)
   A. only plural nouns
   B. only names
   C. only verbs
   D. both countable and uncountable nouns

17. Which quantifier goes with a countable plural noun in a question? (1 mark)
   A. many
   B. much
   C. less
   D. a little

18. Which tense is best for telling the story? (1 mark)
   A. future tense only
   B. past tense
   C. a new tense in each line
   D. no tense

19. What should you do first with a series of pictures? (1 mark)
   A. Copy a friend
   B. Write the ending only
   C. Look at all of them and put them in order
   D. Draw only one

20. Why is it good to write new words and meanings in a notebook while reading? (1 mark)
   A. It replaces reading
   B. It is required by law
   C. It makes the book shorter
   D. It helps you remember them

21. What is a graded reader? (1 mark)
   A. A book written at a level of difficulty suited to certain readers
   B. A test paper
   C. A dictionary
   D. A newspaper advert

22. What is the job of a full stop? (1 mark)
   A. To show a question
   B. To show a list
   C. To show strong feeling
   D. To end a statement or a command

23. How is the sound /v/ made? (1 mark)
   A. The upper teeth touch the lower lip and the voice buzzes
   B. The lips are rounded and do not touch the teeth
   C. The tongue touches the roof and there is no voice
   D. The mouth is closed and air passes through the nose

24. What is the best way to practise a tongue twister? (1 mark)
   A. Read it silently only
   B. Say it as fast as you can straight away
   C. Say it slowly first, then faster
   D. Whisper it once

25. Which is NOT one of the three parts of reading fluency? (1 mark)
   A. Handwriting
   B. Accuracy
   C. Expression
   D. Speed

26. What is the contraction of 'do not'? (1 mark)
   A. do'nt
   B. dont
   C. d'not
   D. don't

27. Which is NOT a way in which HIV spreads? (1 mark)
   A. From a mother to her baby
   B. Through blood
   C. Sharing sharp objects that have blood on them
   D. Sitting together in class

28. Which question is inferential? (1 mark)
   A. What day did Baraka visit the barber?
   B. What did the barber put into his razor?
   C. How did Omondi feel at the start of the story?
   D. Where is the barbershop?

29. What is a riddle? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of song
   B. A long story
   C. A word puzzle that describes something without naming it
   D. A list of rules

30. Which word has the short vowel /ɪ/? (1 mark)
   A. live
   B. leave
   C. seat
   D. feel

31. What is inferring the meaning of a word? (1 mark)
   A. Copying it
   B. Working out its meaning from the words around it
   C. Ignoring it
   D. Spelling it backwards

32. Which word begins with the unvoiced sound /θ/? (1 mark)
   A. the
   B. thank
   C. they
   D. that

33. Which question word asks about ownership? (1 mark)
   A. who
   B. where
   C. whose
   D. when

34. 'Who's' is a short form of which words? (1 mark)
   A. whose is
   B. who has not
   C. who is
   D. who was not

35. Which is the correct spelling of the word meaning 'apart, not together'? (1 mark)
   A. separete
   B. seprate
   C. seperate
   D. separate

36. Which is a sentence in the future tense about tomorrow? (1 mark)
   A. I visit my grandmother now.
   B. Tomorrow I will visit my grandmother.
   C. I was visiting her.
   D. Yesterday I visited my grandmother.

37. Which word has a silent h? (1 mark)
   A. help
   B. hand
   C. honest
   D. house

38. What is a caption? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of advert
   B. The name of the newspaper
   C. A short line that explains a picture
   D. The last paragraph

39. Which is the correct spelling of the evening meal? (1 mark)
   A. diner
   B. dinnner
   C. dinner
   D. dinnar

40. Which is the correct -ing form of 'sit'? (1 mark)
   A. siting
   B. siteing
   C. sitting
   D. sittting

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Write one statement, one WH question and one yes or no question about email. Say how the voice moves in each. (3 marks)

42. Write four sentences about your morning: two with have or has and two with had. (4 marks)

43. Correct the spellings: peple, libary, beutiful. (3 marks)

44. Explain the difference between 'who' and 'whose'. Give one question for each. (3 marks)

45. Write the greeting and closing for a friendly letter to your friend Wanjiku. (2 marks)

46. Write the subject and the object forms of: I, he, we, they. (2 marks)

47. Name three parts of a newspaper. (3 marks)

48. Say whether the voice falls or rises at the end of: (a) Who sent the message? (b) Is the phone on the table? (2 marks)

49. Change to the past progressive: 'The children are singing in the hall.' (2 marks)

50. Change to negative statements: (a) She sells eggs. (b) They picked coffee. (4 marks)

51. Explain what word stress is. Give one example. (2 marks)

52. Explain the proverb 'A stitch in time saves nine'. (2 marks)

53. Replace each plain word with a better describing word: nice room, dirty clothes, good smell. Write the new phrases. (3 marks)

54. Name the five senses and say why a descriptive writer uses them. (3 marks)

55. Write four sentences about your family. Use a, an and the at least once. (4 marks)

56. Explain when we use some and when we use any. Give an example of each. (4 marks)

57. List the three main parts of a composition and say what each does. (3 marks)

58. Arrange in order: (a) Then she paid. (b) Grace entered the shop. (c) Finally, she went home. (2 marks)

59. Write one sentence using 'present' as a noun and one using 'present' as a verb. Show the stress with capital letters. (3 marks)

60. Describe the steps to fill in a form correctly. (4 marks)

61. Copy in neat print: 'Please listen carefully.' Circle the silent letter. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #6 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — fine, vine
   Fine and vine differ only in the first sound, /f/ and /v/.

2. C — The sound guide next to the headword
   Dictionaries show pronunciation beside the headword.

3. D — The women are selling tomatoes.
   Women is plural and takes are.

4. A — boxes
   Nouns ending in x add es.

5. A — please
   Please turns an order into a polite request.

6. D — bed
   Bed has the short vowel /e/.

7. C — after the adjective
   With adjectives, enough comes after the adjective.

8. D — A stick with the round part on its right
   For b the stick is on the left and the round part on the right.

9. A — a circular junction where vehicles go around in one direction
   Traffic moves round a central island.

10. C — Stop, look and listen
   Trains cannot stop quickly.

11. B — understand by looking at it
   Pictures, signs, maps and videos are visuals.

12. D — yours
   Yours stands alone and shows ownership.

13. A — Ali and I went to the clinic.
   I is the subject form.

14. C — Kevin is taller than Musa.
   Use the er form with than.

15. D — I could smell fresh bread.
   It describes something smelt.

16. D — both countable and uncountable nouns
   For example a lot of books and a lot of rain.

17. A — many
   How many books?

18. B — past tense
   Stories are usually told in the past tense.

19. C — Look at all of them and put them in order
   You must understand the whole story first.

20. D — It helps you remember them
   Writing new words helps you remember them.

21. A — A book written at a level of difficulty suited to certain readers
   Graded readers are written at different reading levels.

22. D — To end a statement or a command
   A full stop ends statements and commands.

23. A — The upper teeth touch the lower lip and the voice buzzes
   /v/ uses teeth and lip; /w/ uses rounded lips only.

24. C — Say it slowly first, then faster
   Start slowly to get the sounds right, then speed up.

25. A — Handwriting
   Fluency is accuracy, speed and expression.

26. D — don't
   The apostrophe replaces the o in 'not'.

27. D — Sitting together in class
   Ordinary contact such as sitting together does not spread HIV.

28. C — How did Omondi feel at the start of the story?
   You work out his feelings from clues.

29. C — A word puzzle that describes something without naming it
   The listener guesses the answer.

30. A — live
   'Live' has a short /ɪ/.

31. B — Working out its meaning from the words around it
   Context gives clues.

32. B — thank
   'Thank' has the unvoiced 'th'.

33. C — whose
   'Whose' asks who owns something.

34. C — who is
   Who's = who is (or who has).

35. D — separate
   Remember 'a rat' in separate.

36. B — Tomorrow I will visit my grandmother.
   'Will visit' shows the future.

37. C — honest
   'Honest' is said 'onest'.

38. C — A short line that explains a picture
   A caption describes a picture.

39. C — dinner
   Dinner has a double n.

40. C — sitting
   Sit doubles the t.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: I sent the email (falls). Where is the message? (falls) Did you get it? (rises)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each with correct voice movement.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: I have brushed my teeth. She has swept the floor. We had eaten before we left. He had washed before school.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: people, library, beautiful
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: 'Who' asks about a person: Who is the coach? 'Whose' asks about the owner: Whose ball is this?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for examples.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Dear Wanjiku, ... Yours lovingly, (your name).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the greeting with comma and 1 mark for the closing.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: I, me; he, him; we, us; they, them.
   Working / marking points: Half a mark for each pair.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Masthead (name), headline, byline, article, picture, caption, advert, weather report (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) falls (b) rises
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: The children were singing in the hall.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for were, 1 mark for keeping singing.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: (a) She doesn't sell eggs. (b) They didn't pick coffee.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks each: 1 for the correct helping verb, 1 for the base form of the main verb.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: Word stress is the syllable we say more strongly in a word, for example the first syllable in HOS-pi-tal.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for the example.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: Fixing a small problem early stops it becoming a bigger problem that takes more work.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fixing early and 1 for avoiding bigger work.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: bright, tidy room; muddy, crumpled clothes; fresh smell.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sight, sound, smell, touch and taste. They help the reader to imagine the thing being described.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the senses and 1 for the reason.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: I have a brother. He has an old bicycle. The bicycle is red. We ride it in the yard.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence that uses the articles correctly.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: Some is used in positive sentences and polite offers: I have some books. Any is used in questions and negatives: Do you have any books?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule and 1 mark for each example.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Introduction: tells who, where and when. Body: tells what happened in order. Conclusion: tells how it ended or how the writer felt.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part with its job.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: b, a, c
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for b first and 1 mark for a then c.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: My uncle gave me a PRE-sent. I will pre-SENT the prize to the winner.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence and 1 mark for correct stress.

60. (4 marks)
   Answer: Read the whole form and its instructions, get the facts ready, write neatly in the spaces using block letters if asked, fill every space, check the spelling and sign if needed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct steps.

61. (2 marks)
   Answer: Please listen carefully. (silent t in listen)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for neat copying and 1 mark for identifying t.
